meta.title: Blitz Car Program Work Map
competition: FS Japan (Formula SAE Rules 2026 + FSAEJ local)
meta.architecture: CV: steel spaceframe, single-cylinder, chain + LSD, aero

loops.name: Season loop
loops.description: Post-season review and test data become the starting point of next year's concept. Nothing starts from zero; every target is a delta from the last car.

loops.name: Concept loop
loops.description: Tyre choice, lap sim, mass, engine curve and aero targets are iterated together until the concept converges. Run until a change in one input no longer moves the decision.

loops.name: Hardpoint loop
loops.description: Kinematic hardpoints, chassis pickup nodes, wheel-envelope packaging (upright, brake, hub) and the CAD skeleton trade back and forth. Ends when hardpoints are frozen in TM8.

loops.name: Mass & CG loop
loops.description: Every detailed design reports mass and CG to the budget owner; overruns force redesign or reallocation. Runs continuously through detail design.

loops.name: Load → FEA → redesign
loops.description: Load cases from VD drive component FEA; parts that fail the safety factor or stiffness target go back to geometry. Also catches compliance that ruins kinematics.

loops.name: Aero–cooling–packaging
loops.description: Sidepod and radiator position change aero balance and drag; wing position changes cooling flow; both fight for the same space as driver, engine and harness.

loops.name: Engine tuning loop
loops.description: 1D simulation sets intake and exhaust geometry, the dyno/track measures it, ECU calibration closes the gap, findings feed back to runner and silencer design.

loops.name: Test → setup loop
loops.description: Run, log, analyse, change one thing, run again. Driver feedback and data agree before a setup is accepted.

loops.name: Budget loop
loops.description: Concept ambitions are checked against money and manufacturing capability; long-lead purchases lock decisions early.

activities.title: Rulebook study & rule-owner matrix
activities.why: Every design decision is bounded by two rulebooks: FS Rules (FS UK) and Formula SAE Rules + JSAE local rules (FS Japan). One wrong reading here costs a frame or a scrutineering fail later.
activities.done: Every rule has an owner; compliance checklist exists for each lane; open questions logged with organiser answers.
activities.tools: Shared spreadsheet, PDF annotations, rules Q&A portals
activities.rules: FS: A, T, CV, IN, S, D sections. FSAE: GR, AD, V, F, T, IC, IN, S, D sections + FSAEJ local rules.
tasks: Download both current rulebooks, handbooks and all published FAQs/rule clarifications
Assign every rule section to an owner subteam (rule-owner matrix: section → lane → person)
Build a CV-only compliance checklist per subsystem and keep it as a living sheet
Highlight differences between FS and FSAE rules and design to the stricter one where cheap
Log ambiguous rules and submit rules questions to organisers before design freeze
Brief all subteams in a rules workshop; quiz new members
pitfalls: Designing to last year's rules
Assuming FS and FSAE wording is identical
Local-rule changes published mid-season and nobody re-checks

external_inputs.label: FS Rules 2026 + FS UK handbook; Formula SAE Rules 2026 + FSAEJ participation & local rules

activities.title: Previous car review & lessons-learned intake
activities.why: The fastest gains come from fixing what broke or was slow last year. This turns the old car and its data into concrete targets.
activities.done: Signed Keep / Fix / Change list; each item has an owner lane.
activities.tools: Failure log, event score sheets, data analysis tool
activities.rules: Check eligibility rules for carried-over parts and second-year vehicles at each event.
tasks: Teardown inspection of last car: wear, cracks, loose fasteners, bent parts
Collect judges' feedback from design, cost and business events
List every DNF/failure with root cause (5-why)
Rank issues by points lost and effort to fix
Decide carry-over vs redesign per subsystem
Publish a one-page 'Keep / Fix / Change' sheet to all subteams
pitfalls: Reviews that are opinions without data
Redesigning parts that worked and ignoring ones that failed

activities.title: Vehicle concept & top-level targets
activities.why: Sets the numbers everyone designs to: mass, CG height, wheelbase, track, power, aero yes/no, tyre size. Without frozen targets each subteam optimises its own part and the car does not fit.
activities.done: VRD v1.0 signed and published; all leads acknowledge.
activities.tools: Lap sim results, trade-study matrix, VRD template
activities.rules: Wheelbase, track, displacement and aero dimensional limits from both rulebooks.
tasks: Run concept trade study (aero vs no aero, 10-inch vs 13-inch, wet vs dry sump etc.)
Fix target vehicle mass with driver, CG height, weight distribution
Fix wheelbase and front/rear track envelope
Fix power, torque band and gearing philosophy with Powertrain
Write the Vehicle Requirements Document (VRD): targets + reasons + owner
Sign off VRD with all leads; any later change needs a change request
pitfalls: Targets copied from top teams without your own sim
No change control after VRD

activities.title: Mass, CG & inertia budget
activities.why: Mass and CG are shared resources. A live budget stops the car growing 20 kg heavier one bracket at a time.
activities.done: Budget converged within target at design freeze; weighed car within 3% of predicted.
activities.tools: Spreadsheet linked to CAD mass properties, corner scales
activities.rules: No mass limit in rules; ballast rules apply if used.
tasks: Split total mass target into subsystem allocations
Create budget sheet: part, mass, x/y/z CG, status (estimate/CAD/weighed)
Collect CAD masses weekly; flag overruns in red
Recompute car CG, front/rear split, yaw/roll inertia
Feed updated mass & CG to VD lap sim and load cases
After build: replace estimates with weighed values
pitfalls: Forgetting fasteners, fluids, harness and driver
CG never checked against tilt-test needs

activities.title: Master CAD skeleton & packaging layout
activities.why: A single top-down skeleton (hardpoints, driver template, engine envelope, wheel envelope) lets every subteam design in the right place at the same time.
activities.done: Full car assembled with zero interferences at freeze.
activities.tools: SolidWorks/CATIA/Fusion with PDM or shared drive with version control
activities.rules: Ground clearance, envelope, cockpit template and keep-out zones.
tasks: Build the skeleton model with reference planes, hardpoints, wheel envelopes
Place driver template, engine, fuel tank, radiator, battery, ECU envelopes
Set CAD rules: naming, units, origin, file structure, check-in/out
Run weekly interference checks of full assembly
Maintain the full-car assembly as single source of truth
Publish packaging screenshots after each change
pitfalls: Everyone designs bottom-up and nothing fits
No naming discipline, duplicate files

activities.title: Interface Control Document (ICD)
activities.why: Lists every point where two subteams touch: bolt sizes, loads, connectors, fluid fittings. This is the formal 'who gives what to whom' record.
activities.done: All interfaces 'frozen' before TM8.
activities.tools: Spreadsheet or the team workspace parameter store
activities.rules: Critical fastener rules (grade, positive locking) apply to most interfaces.
tasks: List every physical, electrical and fluid interface between subsystems
For each: owner, receiver, geometry, fastener, load, tolerance, due date
Track status (open / agreed / frozen)
Review open interfaces in every weekly tech meeting
Lock interfaces before design freeze
pitfalls: Interfaces agreed verbally and forgotten
Fastener spec decided at assembly

activities.title: Design reviews (PDR / CDR)
activities.why: Structured reviews catch errors while they are cheap to fix and rehearse the design event at the same time.
activities.done: All CDR actions closed.
activities.rules: Design event criteria (FS S5 / FSAE S design) as the review checklist.
tasks: Preliminary Design Review: concepts, calcs, rule compliance
Critical Design Review: final CAD, FEA, drawings, manufacturing plan
Invite alumni / faculty / industry reviewers
Record action items with owners and due dates
Re-review failed items before freeze
pitfalls: Reviews as presentations with no criticism
Actions never closed

activities.title: Design freeze & drawing release
activities.why: The gate that turns models into parts. After this, changes need a change request so manufacturing can start without chasing a moving target.
activities.done: Release package handed to LOG; change process active.
activities.rules: Submission deadlines for structural documents usually fall near this gate.
tasks: Check every part has a released drawing or purchase spec
Freeze hardpoints and frame geometry first (longest lead)
Issue release packages per subteam to Logistics
Start change-request process (who approves, cost/time impact)
Announce freeze to whole team
pitfalls: Freezing with unchecked drawings
Releasing frame before hardpoints are final

activities.title: Mock scrutineering
activities.why: Inspecting your own car with the official inspection sheet finds the failures before the event does.
activities.done: Two clean mock scrutineerings in a row.
activities.tools: Official inspection sheets, rule checklist, stopwatch, sound meter
activities.rules: FS IN sections (IN7 tilt, IN10 noise, IN11 brake test, egress); FSAE IN sections.
tasks: Print the official inspection sheet for each event (FS UK and FS Japan)
Inspect every item with a non-designer as inspector
Run tilt-table check for fluid leaks if possible
Time driver egress for all drivers
Practice noise test procedure and brake test
Fix-list with owners; repeat mock scrutineering after fixes
pitfalls: Designers inspecting their own parts
Leaving it to the week before shipping

activities.title: Test plan & test-day management
activities.why: Track time is the scarcest resource. A plan with objectives per run turns kilometres into knowledge.
activities.done: Reliability distance achieved; event procedures rehearsed.
activities.tools: Run sheets, setup sheets, failure log
activities.rules: Driving rules (FS D / FSAE D) for practice procedures.
tasks: Write test plan: objectives, runs, setup sheet per run
Shakedown: leaks, brakes, steering, shutdown, then low-speed laps
Reliability mileage target (aim for endurance distance several times over)
Event-specific practice: accel, skidpad, autocross, endurance with driver change
Run a test-day safety briefing; marshal and fire-extinguisher roles
Debrief after every session; log failures and actions
pitfalls: Testing without objectives
Car finished the week before shipping, so no testing

activities.title: Competition technical leadership
activities.why: At the event, one person owns the car's schedule: scrutineering order, fixes, refuelling, dynamic event slots.
activities.done: All tech inspection stickers; car finishes endurance.
activities.rules: Event handbook procedures for each competition.
tasks: Plan scrutineering order and who presents each area
Run fix crew for scrutineering findings
Manage refuelling, tyre and setup changes between events
Keep a timeline of event slots and queues
Make the call on risk (e.g. setup for endurance finish over speed)
pitfalls: Too many people touching the car
No plan for failed inspection items

activities.title: Post-season technical review
activities.why: Closes the season loop. It turns failures, judges' feedback, scores and data into a written starting point for next season, before the seniors who know the answers leave.
activities.done: Review published and archived.
activities.rules: Next year's rule changes noted here.
tasks: Each subteam writes a 2-page review: target vs achieved, failures, ideas
Score sheet analysis: where points were lost
Archive CAD, calcs, data and drawings
Update the rule-owner matrix with new findings
Hand over to TM2 of next season
pitfalls: Seniors leave before writing it down
Blame-focused review that nobody wants to repeat

external_inputs.label: Score sheets from every static and dynamic event

activities.title: Tyre data analysis & tyre/rim selection
activities.why: Tyres set the grip ceiling of the car and the size of the whole wheel envelope (10-inch vs 13-inch). Everything inside the wheel depends on this choice.
activities.done: .tir file + rim/tyre data sheet released.
activities.tools: MATLAB tyre toolset (TTC analysis + MF fitting), MFeval
activities.rules: Wheel size and tyre rules (FS T / FSAE V), dry and wet tyres.
tasks: Run the team MATLAB tyre toolset: compare candidate tyres (Fy, Fx, Mz, load sensitivity)
Check temperature and pressure sensitivity at expected loads
Fit Pacejka Magic Formula and export .tir for lap sim
Choose 10-inch or 13-inch rim; select rim width and offset
Get rim drawing: bolt pattern, centre bore, offset, inner barrel profile
Publish tyre/rim data sheet to VD, BR, AC, TM
pitfalls: Choosing tyres on peak mu alone and ignoring load sensitivity
Rim inner barrel profile unknown until parts arrive

external_inputs.label: FSAE TTC tyre test data (purchased round data)

activities.title: Lap-time simulation & sensitivity
activities.why: Converts design options into competition points. It answers questions like 'is 5 kg worth more than 3 hp?' before any money is spent.
activities.done: Sensitivity report accepted in concept review.
activities.rules: Dynamic event scoring formulas (FS D / FSAE D).
tasks: Build or update a point-mass / quasi-steady-state lap sim
Model each dynamic event and convert times to points
Sensitivity sweep: mass, CG, power, gear ratio, CLA, CDA, track, wheelbase
Produce g-g diagram and peak load estimates for load cases
Report trade-offs to TM3 in points, not seconds
pitfalls: Trusting absolute lap times instead of deltas
No validation against last year's measured laps

external_inputs.label: Event track layouts (accel, skidpad, autocross, endurance)

activities.title: Suspension concept & targets
activities.why: Turns the vehicle targets into suspension numbers: ride frequency, roll gradient, roll centre heights, anti-dive/squat, camber gain, steering behaviour.
activities.done: VD target sheet approved by TM.
activities.rules: Suspension travel and ground clearance rules (FS T / FSAE V).
tasks: Choose architecture: double wishbone, push/pull rod, rocker layout, ARB yes/no
Set ride frequencies and roll gradient
Set roll centre height targets and migration limits
Set camber gain, scrub radius, kingpin, caster, mechanical trail targets
Set anti-dive / anti-squat targets
Document targets in a VD target sheet
pitfalls: Picking geometry first and targets later
Roll centre targets that migrate wildly in roll

activities.title: Suspension kinematics & hardpoints
activities.why: Hardpoints define where every wishbone, pushrod and tie rod mounts. Chassis cannot draw the frame and Upright cannot draw the upright until they exist.
activities.done: Hardpoint table rev A frozen at TM8.
activities.rules: Suspension must have usable travel (rules specify minimum travel with driver).
tasks: Place outboard points inside wheel envelope with clearance to rim and caliper
Place inboard points on/near frame nodes
Iterate to meet roll centre, camber gain, bump steer, anti targets
Check full bump/droop/steer travel for interference
Export hardpoint table (x,y,z) with revision number
Share to CH, TM (CAD skeleton) and VD component designers
pitfalls: Inboard points nowhere near frame nodes
Not checking steer + bump combined

activities.title: Steering geometry & rack selection
activities.why: Sets Ackermann, steering ratio, rack position and tie-rod points. Affects driver effort, turning radius for the hairpins, and bump steer.
activities.done: Rack position and tie-rod points added to hardpoint table.
activities.rules: Steering system rules: positive stops, free play limits, quick-release wheel (FS T / FSAE T).
tasks: Choose Ackermann percentage from tyre slip-angle data
Choose steering ratio (lock-to-lock) for hairpins vs effort
Select rack (bought or custom) and place it
Minimise bump steer by tie-rod point placement
Check steering free-play and stops for rule compliance
pitfalls: Rack fouls the driver's legs or the frame
Too slow ratio for hairpins

external_inputs.label: Tightest hairpin radius from event layouts

activities.title: Load case derivation
activities.why: Every structural part needs forces to design against. VD owns these numbers so all parts are designed to the same events.
activities.done: Load-case sheet rev A issued and used by all FEA.
activities.tools: MATLAB / spreadsheet free-body solver, OptimumK loads
activities.rules: Not directly specified; judges ask for justification of load cases.
tasks: Define load cases: max braking, max cornering, combined, max traction, 3g bump, pothole
Compute tyre contact patch forces per corner per case
Resolve into member forces (wishbones, pushrods, tie rods)
Compute upright, hub and bearing loads
Apply safety factors per part class
Publish load-case sheet to every component designer
pitfalls: Each designer inventing their own loads
Forgetting brake torque reaction and drive torque on hubs

activities.title: Upright design
activities.why: The upright joins wishbones, tie rod, bearings, hub and brake caliper. It is the most interface-heavy part on the car.
activities.done: FEA passes with safety factor; drawing released.
activities.rules: Critical fastener rules for upright pickups.
tasks: Choose material (7075-T6, 6061-T6, steel) and process
Model around bearing seat, pickup points, caliper mounts
Check clearance to rim at full steer and travel
FEA for all load cases; check stiffness (camber compliance)
Topology optimisation if machining allows
Detailed drawing with GD&T on bearing bore and pickup holes
pitfalls: Bearing bore tolerance too loose
Upright fits CAD rim but not real rim

activities.title: Wheel hub & bearing design
activities.why: The hub carries wheel loads into the bearings, holds the brake rotor and, at the rear, takes drive torque from the driveshaft. It needs information from four subteams.
activities.done: Hub drawing released with bearing calc report.
activities.rules: Wheel retention / lug nut rules; positive locking of fasteners (FS T / FSAE V & T).
tasks: Choose bearing type (angular contact pair / deep groove / thin-section) and size from loads and life
Calculate bearing life for the season duty cycle
Design hub: wheel studs or centre lock, rotor flange, spline (rear)
Design bearing preload and retention (nut, spacer, circlip)
FEA hub for combined loads incl. brake torque and drive torque
Drawing with tolerances for bearing fits and spline
pitfalls: Bearing preload not controlled
Spline designed before driveshaft supplier confirmed

activities.title: Wishbones, pushrods, tie rods & inserts
activities.why: The link members carry the load cases into the frame. Buckling, rod-end selection and weld quality decide if they survive.
activities.done: All members pass buckling/stress; jig designed.
activities.rules: Rod end and critical fastener rules; no single-shear on critical joints where rules prohibit.
tasks: Select tube size (steel 4130 or CFRP + bonded inserts) by buckling and stress
Select rod ends / spherical bearings with load rating
Design inserts and adjustable ends (shims, threads for camber/toe)
Design welding jig
Calculate buckling safety factor of pushrods and tie rods
Drawings with cut lengths and weld spec
pitfalls: Rod ends in bending
No adjustment range left for alignment

activities.title: Rockers, dampers, springs & ARB
activities.why: Sets ride and roll stiffness and damping. Motion ratio and damper choice decide how tunable the car is at the track.
activities.done: Spring/damper/ARB spec + rocker drawings released.
activities.rules: Suspension travel rules.
tasks: Calculate motion ratios and wheel rates
Select springs and dampers (adjustable FS-specific dampers)
Design rocker geometry (progression), bearings, pivot
Size and design anti-roll bars (blade or torsion bar)
Create setup sheet ranges for testing
pitfalls: Motion ratio too low, damper never works
Damper ordered late (long lead)

activities.title: Steering system detail design
activities.why: Rack mounts, column, U-joints, quick release and steering wheel. The driver's main control input must be stiff, safe and rule-compliant.
activities.done: Steering assembly drawings released.
activities.rules: Steering wheel quick release, free play, positive stops (FS T / FSAE T).
tasks: Design column with U-joint angles within limits
Select quick release (rules require it)
Design rack mounts and column supports
Steering wheel design with button and shift paddle integration
Check steering free-play and stops
pitfalls: U-joint angles too large → notchy, uneven steering
No clearance check with driver's knees at full lock

activities.title: Suspension compliance & FEA review
activities.why: A good kinematic design is wasted if uprights, brackets and rod ends flex. This step checks the whole corner as one load path and gives judges stiffness numbers, not only stresses.
activities.done: Compliance within target, documented.
tasks: Build a corner compliance model (FEA assembly or spring-network model)
Apply lateral and longitudinal contact-patch loads from VD6
Compute camber and toe compliance (deg per kN)
Find the weakest link (bracket, upright arm, rod end, frame node)
Redesign weakest link and repeat until targets are met
Summarise results in design-event slides
pitfalls: Checking only strength, never stiffness
Ignoring frame-node flex in the corner model

activities.title: Suspension manufacture
activities.why: Wishbones, uprights, hubs and rockers are made or outsourced. Jigs and tolerances decide whether the kinematics match CAD.
activities.done: All suspension parts inspected and labelled.
activities.tools: Jigs, CNC, lathe, welding, measurement tools
tasks: Make wishbone jigs; tack, check, weld
Machine or outsource uprights, hubs, rockers
Press bearings; check preload
Inspect critical dimensions; record measurements
Label parts with part number and side (FL/FR/RL/RR)
pitfalls: Welding distortion not measured
Left/right parts mixed up without labels

activities.title: Corner assembly, alignment & corner weights
activities.why: Puts the car on the ground at the designed setup: ride height, camber, toe, corner weights.
activities.done: Baseline setup sheet recorded; car on its wheels.
activities.tools: Corner scales, camber gauge, toe plates/strings, torque wrench
activities.rules: Positive locking on suspension fasteners.
tasks: Assemble corners with torque spec and positive locking
Set ride height, camber, toe, caster
Corner weight with driver ballast; adjust spring perches
Measure suspension travel and steering stops
Record baseline setup sheet
pitfalls: No baseline recorded, so later changes cannot be compared
Corner weighting without the driver or fuel

activities.title: Setup tuning & K&C validation
activities.why: Confirms the real car behaves like the designed one, then finds the best setup for each event using data and driver feedback together.
activities.done: Setup book ready with data-backed choices.
tasks: Static K&C check: measure camber and toe change through bump and roll
Validate ride frequency and roll gradient from logged data
Compare measured understeer gradient with prediction
Tune ARB, dampers, toe, camber and tyre pressures per event
Build an event setup book (accel, skidpad, autocross, endurance)
Record every change with run number and result
pitfalls: Changing several things at once
Ignoring driver feedback that disagrees with data

activities.title: Design event – VD defence
activities.why: Judges test the reasoning chain from tyre data to targets, geometry and validation. VD usually takes the most questions, and a clear story gains many points.
activities.done: Design event score improved vs last season.
activities.rules: Design event (FS S5 / FSAE S).
tasks: Build a 'why' chain for every key number (from tyre data to setup)
Prepare plots: tyre curves, lap sim sensitivity, kinematics curves, test data
Bring physical parts (upright, hub, rocker)
Prepare honest 'what we would change' answers
Run mock design judging with alumni or faculty
pitfalls: Showing results without reasons
Claiming validation that was never done

activities.title: Chassis rules envelope study
activities.why: The frame is the most rule-dense part of the car: hoops, bracing, side impact, front bulkhead, minimum tube specs. These rules shape the frame before any engineering.
activities.done: Rule-envelope sketch in skeleton; checklist complete.
activities.rules: FS T sections on primary structure; FSAE F (Chassis and Structural).
tasks: Extract all primary/secondary structure rules from FS and FSAE
List minimum tube sizes, alternative tubing and equivalency options
Note main/front hoop geometry, bracing and head-clearance rules
Note side impact, front bulkhead and anti-intrusion requirements
Make a 3D rule-envelope sketch for the CAD skeleton
pitfalls: Using tube sizes from an old rulebook
Missing helmet clearance lines from the start

activities.title: Frame concept & node layout
activities.why: Places frame nodes where suspension, engine and driver loads enter. Good node placement makes a stiff, light frame; bad placement needs heavy tabs.
activities.done: Frame wireframe rev A agreed with VD and ERG.
activities.rules: Hoop geometry, bracing, helmet clearance, cockpit openings.
tasks: Draw wireframe with hoops, bulkhead, side impact members
Put nodes at suspension pickups, engine mounts, harness mounts
Triangulate load paths, especially suspension bays
Check driver template and 95th percentile clearance
Iterate with VD until pickups land on nodes
pitfalls: Suspension pickups mid-tube, causing bending
Cockpit opening too small for the template

activities.title: Tube sizing & torsional stiffness FEA
activities.why: Frame stiffness must be high compared with suspension roll stiffness so the springs do the work. Mass must stay in budget.
activities.done: Stiffness target met at mass target.
activities.rules: Minimum tube specs; equivalency calculations.
tasks: Beam-element FEA for torsional stiffness (Nm/deg)
Load-case FEA for cornering, braking, bump
Optimise tube sizes within rule minimums
Check stiffness ratio frame vs suspension roll stiffness
Report mass and CG to TM4
pitfalls: Optimising with tubes the rules do not allow
Comparing stiffness with no suspension roll stiffness target

activities.title: Structural equivalency submission (SES / structural docs)
activities.why: Organisers must approve the structure before you build it. A rejected submission blocks the whole car.
activities.done: Approved by both competitions.
activities.rules: FS A5 documentation deadlines; FSAE structural documentation requirements.
tasks: Fill the structural spreadsheet/template for each competition
Provide drawings and photos required
Document any alternative materials or tube sizes
Submit before the deadline; answer reviewer questions
Keep approved version for scrutineering
pitfalls: Template version mismatch
Built frame differs from submitted one

external_inputs.label: Official structural equivalency spreadsheet/template for each event

activities.title: Impact attenuator & anti-intrusion plate
activities.why: Protects the driver's feet in a frontal crash. Use the standard attenuator or prove a custom one by test data.
activities.done: IA approved; mounting drawing released.
activities.rules: Impact attenuator & anti-intrusion rules (FS T / FSAE F), IAD submission.
tasks: Decide standard IA vs custom attenuator
Design anti-intrusion plate and bolted/welded mounting to the front bulkhead
Check IA fits inside the nose with clearance
Prepare the IA data report for each competition
Order standard IA early if chosen (long lead)
pitfalls: Bolt pattern not matching the bulkhead
Nose designed without IA envelope

external_inputs.label: Standard IA spec or custom IA test requirements

activities.title: Mounting brackets & tabs (all subsystems)
activities.why: Every subsystem bolts to the frame. Chassis owns the tabs so welding happens once, before paint.
activities.done: All tabs on the frame drawing; nothing to weld after paint.
activities.rules: Harness attachment, critical fastener and bracket rules.
tasks: Collect all mount requests through the ICD
Design tabs with correct thickness and double shear where required
FEA the suspension and harness brackets
Add tabs to the frame weldment drawing
Freeze tab list before welding
pitfalls: Tabs requested after welding and painting
Single-shear tabs where double shear is needed

activities.title: Frame jig & tube drawings
activities.why: Frame accuracy decides whether the hardpoints in the welded frame match the hardpoints VD designed. The jig and drawings are where that accuracy is built in.
activities.done: Jig and tube drawings released to workshop.
activities.tools: CAD, notching templates, cut list sheet
tasks: Design frame jig (laser-cut plates, fixture table or tube jig)
Create cut list with tube lengths, grades and notch angles
Generate printable coping/notching templates
Plan the weld sequence to limit distortion
Add datum features for measuring hardpoints later
pitfalls: No datum features for measuring later
Cut list not updated after last CAD change

activities.title: Frame fabrication & welding
activities.why: Turns the design into the backbone of the car. Weld quality is inspected at scrutineering.
activities.done: Frame fully welded with measurement record.
activities.rules: Material certificates may be requested at inspection.
tasks: Cut and notch tubes
Tack frame in jig; measure diagonals and node positions
Weld in planned sequence (TIG)
Weld all tabs
Record measurements and any deviations
pitfalls: Welding without measuring between stages
Wrong wall thickness tube used

activities.title: Frame inspection & torsion test
activities.why: Proves the real frame matches CAD (hardpoints) and FEA (stiffness) before the rest of the car is built on it. Also gives the design event real validation data.
activities.done: Deviation and stiffness report signed off.
activities.tools: Torsion rig, dial gauges, measuring arm or tape and plumb
tasks: Measure hardpoint locations vs CAD
Torsion test with dial gauges
Compare with FEA; explain differences
Inspect welds; fix defects
Release frame for paint/assembly
pitfalls: Skipping the torsion test and having no validation for judges
Finding hardpoint errors after suspension is assembled

activities.title: Firewall, floor & closeout panels
activities.why: The firewall separates the driver from fuel and engine; the floor closeout stops the driver touching the ground. Both are rule items inspected at scrutineering.
activities.done: Panels drawn; pass-throughs sealed.
activities.rules: Firewall and floor closeout rules (FS T / FSAE T).
tasks: Design firewall covering the area required by rules
Design sealed grommets for harness, cables and hoses passing through
Design floor closeout panels
Choose materials that meet the rules
Plan quick-release fasteners for removable panels
Send mounting tab needs to CH6
pitfalls: Gaps around harness pass-throughs
Firewall too low near the driver's head

activities.title: Paint / powder coat & finishing
activities.why: Coating protects the steel from corrosion and makes cracks easier to see. It is done only after every tab is welded and the frame passes inspection.
activities.done: Frame coated and returned.
tasks: Confirm no more tabs are needed (CH6 frozen)
Mask threads, bearing seats and mating faces
Powder coat or paint, using livery colours
Chase threads; clean mating faces
Record coating mass for TM4
pitfalls: Coating inside bearing bores or threads
Coating before all tabs are welded

activities.title: Driver anthropometry & template study
activities.why: Rules require the car to fit a 95th percentile template, and your real drivers must fit, see and egress quickly.
activities.done: Driver data sheet + template model.
activities.rules: 95th percentile template and cockpit rules.
tasks: Model the rules template in CAD
Measure all candidate drivers (height, sitting height, leg and arm length)
Find smallest and largest driver to set adjustment range
Set cockpit targets: sight lines, elbow, knee and helmet clearance
Share driver data with Chassis and VD
pitfalls: Designing for one driver
Ignoring helmet and gloves in clearances

activities.title: Cockpit packaging & driver position
activities.why: Driver position sets the car's CG height, the frame shape, steering wheel and pedal positions. It is one of the first things to fix in the skeleton.
activities.done: Driver position frozen and in skeleton.
activities.rules: Cockpit opening, internal cross-section, visibility rules.
tasks: Choose seat angle and hip point
Place steering wheel, pedals, shifter
Build a wooden or tube cockpit buck
Test with real drivers; adjust
Publish driver template in CAD skeleton
pitfalls: Driver too upright, raising CG
Steering wheel blocks egress

activities.title: Seat & headrest
activities.why: A seat that holds the driver firmly gives steadier inputs; the headrest must meet head-restraint rules. Inserts let several drivers share the car.
activities.done: Seat drawings and moulds ready.
activities.rules: Head restraint and seat rules.
tasks: Make foam-bag seat moulds of each driver
Design composite seat or moulded insert system
Design headrest with rule-compliant energy-absorbing foam
Design seat mounting to frame nodes
Plan quick insert swap for driver change
pitfalls: Seat blocks egress
Headrest foam not the type the rules require

activities.title: Harness & mounting
activities.why: Harness geometry and mounting are strictly defined in the rules and inspected closely. Mounts also need frame tabs welded before paint.
activities.done: Mount positions in CH6 tab list.
activities.rules: Driver restraint system rules (angles, mounts, certification date).
tasks: Select a certified harness within its valid date
Design shoulder, lap and anti-submarine belt mounts
Check belt angles with the template in CAD
Send mount positions and loads to CH6
Plan harness adjustment for different drivers
pitfalls: Expired harness labels
Shoulder belt angle outside rules for tall drivers

activities.title: Pedal box & driver controls
activities.why: Brake pedal ratio sets brake feel; throttle feel and travel affect drivability. Shared with Braking.
activities.done: Pedal box drawings released.
activities.rules: Brake pedal load requirement, throttle return springs, over-travel switch.
tasks: Design pedal tray with adjustment range
Design brake pedal with balance bar mounts
Design throttle pedal with return springs (two springs)
FEA brake pedal for rule-specified pedal force
Add stops and over-travel switch mount
pitfalls: Pedal too weak for the rule pedal force
Pedal box adjustment that slips under load

activities.title: Shifter, switches & cockpit controls
activities.why: Gear shift, shutdown buttons and master switches must be reachable and correctly marked. Poor placement fails inspection or slows the driver.
activities.done: Controls positions agreed with ECS.
activities.rules: Shutdown buttons, master switch location and marking.
tasks: Choose shift system (mechanical lever, pneumatic, electric)
Place the cockpit shutdown button within reach with belts tight
Place master switches where marshals can reach them
Label switches as the rules require
Design mounts and request tabs from CH6
pitfalls: Kill switch out of driver reach
Shifter fouling the frame

activities.title: Seat fitting & egress drills
activities.why: Every driver must get out of the car within the rule time with full gear. Practice also finds snags in seat, wheel and harness.
activities.done: All drivers below required time with margin.
activities.rules: Driver egress test.
tasks: Fit each driver with their seat insert
Practice egress with full gear (helmet, gloves, suit)
Time each driver; record results
Fix snags (wheel release, belt buckle, insert edges)
Repeat until all drivers pass with margin
pitfalls: Not practising with gloves and helmet
Only testing the smallest driver

activities.title: Engine selection & baseline
activities.why: The single-cylinder engine sets power, mass, packaging, heat load and reliability for the whole season. It is also the longest-lead purchase, so it must be decided early.
activities.done: Engine purchased; engine data sheet (bore, stroke, valve timing, ratios, mass) published.
activities.rules: FS CV1 / FSAE IC: four-stroke, displacement limit, single air restrictor between throttle and engine.
tasks: List single-cylinder candidates within the displacement limit (450–690 cc motocross/enduro/street engines)
Compare peak power, torque band, dry mass, gearbox ratios, starter, cooling, wet/dry sump
Check aftermarket ECU / injector / throttle body support
Check spares price, rebuild interval, availability of a service manual
Decide carry-over engine vs new; plan spare engine or rebuild kit
Order engine and long-lead spares; record serial numbers
pitfalls: Choosing peak power over reliability and torque band
No rebuild plan, so engine runs tired at competition

external_inputs.label: Displacement, four-stroke, restrictor and fuel rules

activities.title: Engine 1D simulation & torque targets
activities.why: With a restrictor fitted, intake and exhaust lengths decide where torque lives. The simulation gives VD a realistic torque curve and Aero & Cooling the heat to reject.
activities.done: Target torque curve + intake/exhaust geometry released.
activities.tools: GT-Power, Ricardo WAVE, Lotus Engine Simulation
activities.rules: Restrictor: 20 mm for gasoline, 19 mm for E85 in recent FS/FSAE rules — confirm in current rulebook.
tasks: Build 1D model of engine + restrictor + plenum + runner + exhaust
Sweep runner length, plenum volume and exhaust primary length
Choose torque band vs gearing with lap sim (VD2)
Output torque curve, volumetric efficiency, fuel flow
Estimate heat rejection to coolant and oil for cooling sizing
Publish the target torque curve and geometry
pitfalls: Uncalibrated model treated as truth
Optimising peak power the car cannot use

external_inputs.label: Restrictor diameter and position

activities.title: Intake: restrictor, plenum, runner, throttle
activities.why: The restrictor chokes airflow; the venturi, plenum and runner design decide how much power and throttle response survive.
activities.done: Intake drawings released; leak-test plan written.
activities.rules: Restrictor location (throttle → restrictor → engine order), intake system location rules (FS CV1 / FSAE IC).
tasks: CFD the converging-diverging restrictor for minimum loss
Design plenum and runner; check volume vs sim
Select throttle body; design throttle cable route
Choose manufacture (SLS/SLA print, CFRP, aluminium) and check heat resistance
Add bosses for MAP, IAT, injector
Plan leak test (pressure/vacuum)
pitfalls: Leak between restrictor and engine = instant fail
Printed plenum softening with heat

activities.title: Exhaust & silencer
activities.why: Exhaust tuning adds torque; the silencer must pass the noise test at the event with margin.
activities.done: Exhaust drawings released with heat shield plan.
activities.rules: FS CV3 exhaust & noise control; FSAE IC exhaust/noise. Noise test at inspection (FS IN10).
tasks: Design header with correct primary length and collector
Select or design silencer (packing, volume)
Plan O2 sensor boss for ECS
Design heat shielding near harness, fuel and composites
Check outlet height/position rules
Plan noise test rehearsal
pitfalls: Passing noise when new, failing after packing burns out
Exhaust cooking harness or bodywork

external_inputs.label: Noise test procedure and limits, outlet position

activities.title: Fuel system: tank, pump, lines, filler
activities.why: The fuel system must feed the engine in hard cornering without starving, and must not leak during the tilt test.
activities.done: Fuel system drawings and fittings list released.
activities.rules: Fuel system location, filler neck, sight tube, venting rules; tilt test (FS IN7).
tasks: Size tank volume for endurance + margin
Design tank with baffles or a surge pot for lateral g
Select pump, regulator, filter
Route lines with rule-compliant fittings and protection
Design filler neck, sight tube and vent
Plan pressure and tilt leak tests
pitfalls: Starvation at low fuel in long corners
Lines routed near exhaust

external_inputs.label: Fuel tank, filler, venting, line and tilt rules

activities.title: Gearing, chain & sprockets
activities.why: Final drive ratio decides acceleration and how much of the torque curve is used on the track.
activities.done: Gear set and guard drawings released.
activities.rules: Chain/scatter shield rules (FS T / FSAE T).
tasks: Choose final drive ratio per event (accel vs endurance)
Select chain size and sprockets; check chain loads
Design chain guard to rules
Design chain tension adjustment (eccentric diff carriers)
Specify spare sprockets for event changes
pitfalls: No tension adjustment designed in
Guard too thin for rules

activities.title: Limited-slip differential & carriers
activities.why: The LSD controls traction on corner exit; its carriers take chain pull and must allow chain adjustment.
activities.done: LSD spec and carrier drawings released.
tasks: Select LSD (torque-sensing or plate type) and preload
Design diff carriers with eccentric adjustment
FEA carriers with chain pull + drive torque
Design sprocket mount to diff
Request mounting tabs from Chassis
pitfalls: Carriers flex and the chain jumps
No way to adjust chain tension

activities.title: Driveshafts & tripod joints
activities.why: Transfers torque to the rear hubs through full suspension travel; its spline is a direct interface with the hub.
activities.done: Driveshaft drawings released; spline spec agreed with VD8.
tasks: Select tripod joints and housings
Check plunge and angle over full travel + steer
Size shaft for torsional stress and fatigue
Define hub-side spline spec and send to VD8
Design boots and retention
pitfalls: Plunge runs out at full droop
Spline designed twice by two teams

activities.title: Engine mounts & packaging
activities.why: Engine mounts hold the engine against drive and shift loads and decide how low it sits. Engine height is one of the largest single CG items.
activities.done: Mount drawings released; engine CG reported.
tasks: Position the engine as low as oil pan and exhaust allow
Design mounts (plate or tube) to frame nodes
FEA for drive torque, gear-shift and bump loads
Plan rubber isolation if vibration is a problem
Report engine and drivetrain mass and CG to TM4
pitfalls: Vibration cracks at welds
Mounts that block engine removal

activities.title: Lubrication & oil system
activities.why: Sustained lateral g can starve a wet sump and destroy the engine. Catch cans and breathers are rule items.
activities.done: Oil system drawings released.
activities.rules: Catch can and breather rules.
tasks: Decide wet sump with baffles vs dry sump
Check oil pickup under sustained lateral g
Design catch cans and breather routing
Decide oil cooler need with Aero & Cooling
Design oil fill and drain access
pitfalls: Oil starvation in skidpad
Breather vent dripping on exhaust

activities.title: Powertrain manufacture & procurement
activities.why: Makes and buys every powertrain part on time and inspects it before assembly, so first fire is not delayed by a missing fitting.
activities.done: Complete powertrain kit inspected and labelled.
tasks: Order injector, throttle body, fuel pump, fittings
Make intake, exhaust, mounts, diff carriers
Inspect or rebuild the engine; record clearances
Inspect every part against its drawing
Label and store parts by assembly order
pitfalls: Late imported parts stop first fire
Engine rebuilt without recording clearances

activities.title: Engine dyno & base calibration
activities.why: Measures real torque, closes the loop with the simulation and produces a safe base map before the car runs on track.
activities.done: Base map validated; measured torque curve published.
activities.tools: Engine/chassis dyno, wideband lambda, ECU software
tasks: Run engine on dyno (or chassis dyno / in-car with logging)
Map fuel (lambda) and ignition per rpm/load
Measure torque curve vs PT2 prediction
Test cooling and oil temperatures under load
Feed results back to PT2 and VD2
pitfalls: No dyno access, so the map is built on track only
Running lean during dyno pulls

activities.title: Powertrain install & first fire
activities.why: The engine running inside the car is the first big assembly milestone. It also proves fuel, cooling, electrics and shutdown work together.
activities.done: Engine runs in car; no leaks.
activities.rules: Shutdown must kill the engine (ECS7).
tasks: Install engine, mounts, diff, chain, driveshafts
Fill and bleed coolant; fill oil
Install fuel system; pressure-test lines
First fire with fire extinguisher ready
Check leaks, temperatures, shutdown function
pitfalls: Fuel leaks found with a hot engine
No fire extinguisher ready at first fire

activities.title: Noise test & tilt rehearsal
activities.why: Noise and tilt are pass/fail tests at inspection. Rehearsing them makes the event a formality and leaves time to fix a silencer.
activities.done: Measured noise below limit with margin.
activities.tools: Sound level meter, tilt table if available
activities.rules: Noise test (FS IN10), tilt test (FS IN7); FSAE IN equivalents.
tasks: Measure noise at idle and at the rule test rpm
Repack or modify the silencer if close to the limit
Fill fuel to rule level; tilt check for leaks
Check catch cans and breathers during tilt
Record results for the scrutineering file
pitfalls: Testing noise only with a cold engine
Silencer packing burning out over the season

external_inputs.label: Noise test rpm and limits; tilt procedure

activities.title: Aero concept & targets
activities.why: Decides how much downforce and drag the car carries and where the centre of pressure sits. Feeds lap sim and load cases.
activities.done: Aero targets in VRD.
activities.tools: Lap sim, hand calcs, past CFD
activities.rules: Aerodynamic device rules (FS T / FSAE T): position, height, width limits.
tasks: Decide package: front wing, rear wing, undertray/diffuser, sidepods
Set CLA, CDA and aero balance (% front) targets
Estimate aero mass
Feed coefficients to lap sim
Estimate peak downforce for load cases
pitfalls: Aero balance not matched to mechanical balance
Aero mass ignored in the lap sim

external_inputs.label: Aero device dimension and position limits

activities.title: Cooling system sizing
activities.why: An overheating engine ends endurance. Radiator size and position fight aero and packaging.
activities.done: Radiator spec and envelope released.
activities.rules: Coolant and overflow rules (water-only coolant where specified).
tasks: Calculate heat to reject at worst case
Size radiator core and fan
Choose position (sidepod, behind driver)
Estimate airflow through duct
Plan coolant routing and overflow
pitfalls: Sizing for cool UK weather and overheating in Japan's summer heat
Fan not considered for slow autocross sections

external_inputs.label: Ambient temperatures at FS Japan and FS UK

activities.title: Aero CFD & package design
activities.why: Turns the aero targets into wing profiles and surfaces, with downforce, drag and balance checked across ride height and yaw.
activities.done: Aero package frozen.
activities.rules: Aero device dimensions.
tasks: Select wing profiles and element counts
Full-car CFD at straight and cornering conditions
Check sensitivity to ride height and yaw
Iterate for balance
Report final CLA, CDA, balance, mass
pitfalls: CFD never validated on track
Package sensitive to ride height changes

activities.title: Wing mounts & aero structures
activities.why: Wings must stay attached, stay stable and not deflect beyond the rules under load. Mounts also add mass high up, so they matter for CG.
activities.done: Mount drawings released.
activities.rules: Aero device stability and deflection rules.
tasks: Design wing mounts, pylons and endplates
FEA under peak aero load plus inertia and bump loads
Check deflection against rule limits
Design adjustment for wing angle
Request mounting tabs from CH6
pitfalls: Wing flutter at speed
Mounts too weak for a cone strike

activities.title: Bodywork, nose cone & sidepods
activities.why: Bodywork covers the frame, wraps the impact attenuator, carries sponsor branding and guides air into the radiator and around the driver.
activities.done: Bodywork surfaces and panel drawings released.
activities.rules: Bodywork, sharp edge and opening rules; visibility of switches and numbers.
tasks: Surface nose, sidepods and engine cover from the CAD skeleton
Split into removable panels with quick fasteners for service
Leave cut-outs/access for master switches, filler neck, jacking
Plan mould split lines and draft angles
Check all edges against minimum radius rules
Export flat logo areas to Business & Brand
pitfalls: Sharp edges fail inspection
Panels that need 20 minutes to remove at the event

activities.title: Cooling installation design
activities.why: Ducts, hoses, fan and overflow decide whether the sized radiator actually gets air and coolant.
activities.done: Cooling installation drawings and hose list released.
activities.rules: Coolant type and overflow/catch rules.
tasks: Design inlet and outlet ducts with sealed sides so air cannot bypass the core
Route hoses with minimum bends; select clamps and fittings
Place expansion/overflow bottle to rules
Mount fan with shroud; agree fan control with ECS
Add coolant temperature sensor bosses
Design radiator mounts with vibration isolation
pitfalls: Air leaking around the core
Hoses chafing on frame

activities.title: Composite manufacture & cooling procurement
activities.why: Makes moulds, wings and bodywork, and buys the radiator, fan and hoses. Composite parts take weeks, so they must start right after release.
activities.done: Aero and cooling parts ready for fit-up.
activities.tools: Composites shop, vacuum bagging, oven if available
tasks: Machine or build plugs and moulds (MDF/foam/tooling board)
Layup wings, endplates, bodywork; cure; trim
Bond inserts for mounts
Procure radiator, fan, hoses, clamps
Weigh parts and report to TM4
Inspect surface finish and fit on frame
pitfalls: Moulds started late, so bodywork arrives after testing
Poor mould finish needing hours of sanding

activities.title: Aero & cooling validation
activities.why: Confirms the real downforce, drag and cooling performance so the setup and future designs rest on data.
activities.done: Validation report: predicted vs measured.
tasks: Coastdown test for drag
Suspension-displacement or load-based downforce estimate at speed
Wool tufts / flow-vis paint on wings and sidepods
Log coolant and oil temperatures across endurance runs
Compare with predictions; adjust wing angles
pitfalls: No baseline run without aero to compare
Temperatures logged only on cool days

activities.title: Braking targets & brake force distribution
activities.why: Sets the deceleration target and the ideal front/rear split from load transfer. Every brake component is sized from these numbers.
activities.done: Braking target sheet approved.
activities.rules: Brake test requires locking all four wheels (FS IN11 / FSAE IN).
tasks: Compute dynamic axle loads at target deceleration
Plot ideal brake force distribution curve
Choose design bias with margin to avoid rear lock first
Define target pedal force and pedal travel
Publish braking target sheet
pitfalls: Bias computed with static CG only
Ignoring downforce at braking speed

activities.title: Brake component sizing
activities.why: Picks calipers, rotors, master cylinders, pedal ratio and balance bar. Caliper and rotor size decide the space VD has inside the wheel.
activities.done: Component spec sheet released.
activities.rules: Two independent hydraulic circuits; brake system rules (FS T / FSAE T).
tasks: Choose caliper (piston area) per axle
Size rotor diameter and thickness; estimate temperature over endurance
Choose master cylinder bores front/rear and pedal ratio
Check line pressure and pedal travel
Specify balance bar and adjustment range
Send caliper and rotor envelope to VD4/VD7
pitfalls: Caliper that fouls the 10-inch rim barrel
Pedal ratio too low, needing huge pedal force

external_inputs.label: Dual-circuit and brake system rules

activities.title: Rotor & mounting design
activities.why: Rotor must handle heat and mount to the hub. The mounting pattern is a direct input to the hub design.
activities.done: Rotor drawing and mounting spec released.
tasks: Design rotor (laser cut steel, floating or fixed)
Design drilling/slotting for mass and pad cleaning
Define mounting PCD, bolt size, bobbins if floating
Thermal and stress check
Send mounting spec to hub designer
pitfalls: Rotor warping from no thermal expansion allowance
Mounting PCD changed after hub drawing release

activities.title: Caliper mounting & brake lines
activities.why: Caliper mounting on the upright and line routing affect pedal stiffness, bleeding and safety. Bleed screws must end up at the top.
activities.done: Mounting and line routing drawings released.
activities.rules: Line protection and mounting rules.
tasks: Define caliper mounting points on upright
Design spacers and shims for alignment
Route hard and flexible lines with protection
Position bleed nipples at the top
Specify fittings
pitfalls: Bleed screws at the bottom
Flexible lines rubbing on wheels at full steer

activities.title: Brake light & over-travel switch
activities.why: The brake light and brake over-travel switch are rule-required safety items. They link the pedal box with the shutdown circuit, so Braking and ECS must agree on them.
activities.done: Switch positions in pedal drawings.
activities.rules: Brake light and brake over-travel switch rules.
tasks: Select brake pressure switch for the brake light
Design over-travel switch position on the pedal box
Agree wiring and logic with ECS
Test switch trigger point on the bench
Document for scrutineering
pitfalls: Switch triggers during normal hard braking
Brake light too dim in daylight

activities.title: Brake installation, bleeding & bedding
activities.why: A firm, consistent pedal comes from clean assembly, correct bleeding and bedded pads; inspectors push hard on the pedal.
activities.done: Firm pedal, no leaks, run-out within limit.
activities.tools: Bleed kit, dial gauge, torque wrench, pressure gauges
activities.rules: Brake system inspection items (dual circuit, reservoirs, line protection).
tasks: Install master cylinders, balance bar, reservoirs
Fit calipers with spacers; check rotor centring and run-out
Install lines; torque fittings; leak-check under pressure
Bleed each circuit (furthest corner first)
Bed in pads and rotors with a defined procedure
Set initial balance bar position from BR1
pitfalls: Air trapped because bleed screws face down
Wrong fluid or contaminated pads

activities.title: Brake test rehearsal & bias tuning
activities.why: The brake test is pass/fail and requires all four wheels to lock. Bias also changes lap time and driver confidence.
activities.done: Repeatable 4-wheel lock; bias documented.
activities.tools: Line pressure sensors, wheel speed data
activities.rules: Brake test (FS IN11 / FSAE IN).
tasks: Practice the brake test sequence from the rulebook
Adjust balance bar until all four lock reliably
Log front/rear pressure; compare with BR1 prediction
Check pad and rotor temperatures after endurance runs
Write brake test procedure card for drivers
pitfalls: Rears will not lock because bias is too far forward
Bias set cold and never re-checked hot

activities.title: Electrical architecture & shutdown circuit
activities.why: Defines every electrical device, power supply and the rule-required shutdown circuit. All other electrical work follows this.
activities.done: Architecture and shutdown schematic approved.
activities.rules: CV electrical, master switch, shutdown buttons and brake light rules — check FS CV and FSAE IC/T electrical sections.
tasks: Make a block diagram of all electrical devices
Design shutdown circuit: master switch, shutdown buttons, inertia switch, BOTS
Define power budget and fuse/relay layout
Pick connector family and wire gauges
Write the electrical system description for inspection
pitfalls: Shutdown circuit not killing fuel pump and ignition
No fuse for each circuit

activities.title: ECU selection & sensor plan
activities.why: The ECU runs the engine and often logs data; its inputs decide which sensors Powertrain must package.
activities.done: ECU and sensor list frozen.
tasks: Choose a standalone ECU or modified OEM ECU
List sensors: crank, cam, MAP, IAT, TPS, lambda, coolant, oil, fuel pressure
Decide CAN bus layout to dash and logger
Send sensor positions to PT3, PT4, PT5
Check ECU support for shift cut and launch control
pitfalls: ECU without enough inputs
No support or tuning knowledge locally

activities.title: Wiring harness design
activities.why: The harness connects every sensor, actuator and switch. Most race-weekend failures are wiring, so routing, protection and labelling matter as much as the schematic.
activities.done: Harness drawing released.
activities.rules: Wiring protection rules.
tasks: Draw wiring diagram pin-to-pin
Route harness in CAD; measure lengths
Choose sleeving and strain relief
Plan service loops and labels
Report harness mass
pitfalls: Harness routed near the exhaust
Connectors that cannot be unplugged without tools

activities.title: Battery, LV power, fuses & relays
activities.why: Low-voltage power must start the engine and run pump, fan, ECU and logger reliably through a long endurance run with a hot restart.
activities.done: Power distribution design released.
activities.rules: Battery mounting and protection rules.
tasks: Size battery for cranking and run time
Design power distribution (fuse box or PDM)
Check charging from the engine stator/alternator
Design battery mount and protection to rules
Plan hot-restart test for endurance driver change
pitfalls: Battery flat after a few starts
Battery not secured to rules

activities.title: Dashboard, steering-wheel electronics & shift
activities.why: The driver interface: shift lights, gear display, warnings and buttons. A failed wheel connector can end a run.
activities.done: Wheel and dash electronics working on the bench.
activities.tools: KiCad, dash configuration software, bench power supply
activities.rules: Steering wheel must remove with quick release; wiring must not hinder it.
tasks: Choose dash or build a CAN display; define warning pages (oil P, water T, low fuel, low battery)
Design steering-wheel PCB, buttons, paddle switches
Choose quick-release connector that survives repeated removal
Design shift actuator control (ignition cut / blip if supported)
Define shift-light rpm per gear from PT2 torque curve
Bench-test the wheel before installation
pitfalls: Wheel connector failing after 50 removals
Warnings nobody can read while driving

activities.title: Harness manufacture
activities.why: Building the harness on a board, away from the car, makes it faster to install and far more reliable.
activities.done: Harness passes 100% continuity check; as-built drawing updated.
tasks: Build a 1:1 harness board from CAD lengths
Crimp with correct tools; pull-test sample crimps
Label every wire and connector both ends
Heat-shrink and sleeve branches; add strain relief
Continuity and insulation check every circuit
Document as-built changes
pitfalls: Cheap crimpers causing intermittent faults
No labels, so faults take hours to trace

activities.title: Electrical install & shutdown functional test
activities.why: Gets the car electrically alive and proves every rule-required safety function before the engine runs.
activities.done: Signed electrical sign-off sheet.
activities.rules: Shutdown circuit, master switch, brake light inspection items.
tasks: Install harness; clip every 150-200 mm; protect at edges
Power up in stages: dash, ECU, sensors, pump, ignition
Test every shutdown button, master switch, inertia switch and BOTS kills the engine
Test brake light brightness and visibility
Check all sensor readings make sense
Record the test on a sign-off sheet
pitfalls: Shutdown kills ignition but fuel pump keeps running
Harness pinched by bodywork

activities.title: ECU base map & calibration
activities.why: A safe base map lets the engine start and run; track calibration then improves drivability and fuel use.
activities.done: Calibrated map + backup copies saved.
tasks: Configure ECU: trigger, injector data, sensor calibrations
Build start-up and idle map
Create safe rev limit and cold-start settings
Tune fuel and ignition on dyno, then on track
Tune throttle response for drivability
Set up logging channels for engine health
pitfalls: Running lean at full load
No backup of the working map

activities.title: Data acquisition plan & channel list
activities.why: Decides what the car will measure. Sensors must be designed in now; adding them after build means drilling and splicing.
activities.done: Channel list frozen and in ICD.
tasks: Collect what each subteam wants to prove with data
Write channel list: sensor, range, sample rate, location, owner
Choose logger (ECU internal, dash logger, standalone)
Prioritise: must-have (engine safety, speed, g, steering, brakes) vs nice-to-have
Send sensor mounting needs to designers via ICD
pitfalls: Sensors chosen after the parts are made
Logging at too low a sample rate

activities.title: Logger & telemetry setup
activities.why: Logger hardware and software must be set up and tested before the car runs, so the first shakedown already gives usable data.
activities.done: Bench logging verified on all channels.
tasks: Configure logger channels, scaling and sample rates
Calibrate sensors (steering, damper pots, pressure)
Set up live telemetry radio if used
Bench-test full logging chain
Create a data file naming and backup routine
pitfalls: Unscaled channels, so nobody knows what the numbers mean
Data lost because nobody backed it up

activities.title: Driver selection & training programme
activities.why: Driver skill is one of the cheapest sources of points. Training must start long before the car exists.
activities.done: Driver pool selected; training log started.
activities.tools: Karting track, sim rig, lap timers
activities.rules: Driver requirements in both rulebooks.
tasks: Select a driver pool (at least 4 for event and endurance changes)
Karting and simulator sessions with lap timing
Teach FS event formats and rules (flags, cones, driver change)
Collect body measurements for ergonomics
Rank drivers per event type
pitfalls: Only one experienced driver
Drivers chosen by seniority, not by lap times

external_inputs.label: Candidate drivers' experience

activities.title: Data analysis toolchain
activities.why: Raw logs are useless without math channels and standard reports that every subteam can read quickly after a run.
activities.done: Report templates working on sample data.
tasks: Create math channels: roll gradient, understeer gradient, slip, lap time
Build a standard report per run (engine health, brakes, VD)
Write a short guide for each subteam
Set up comparison overlays between drivers
Train at least two people to use the tools
pitfalls: Only one person can read the data
Reports so long nobody reads them

activities.title: Test data & driver coaching loop
activities.why: Turns every test run into setup decisions and better drivers. Without this loop, testing only adds kilometres.
activities.done: Data archive with debrief notes per session.
tasks: Download and back up data after each run
Produce the standard report within minutes
Debrief drivers with data overlays
Feed findings to VD15, BR7, AC8, ECS8
